newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wary Australian stocks end lower, watching Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Wary Australian stocks end lower, watching Wall St.

text.p: SPI futures 2360 -26 US 30yr cl 7.11 +0.01
10yrbond futs 92.015 -0.010 Gold NY 348.65 Lon fix 347.60
S&P500(Globex) 763.35 steady NZSE40 2232.98 -0.87
*Stocks settle lower by end, little changed from noon levels as market awaits U.S. inflation data. Volume 283.15 million, value A$759.73 million, 1,030 stocks traded, 342 steady, 270 up, 418 down.
The Australian share market ended lower on Friday as cautious traders cut positions ahead of Wall Street's reaction to U.S. inflation data due later today.
By 4.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 12.4 points at 2,380.5.
June share price index futures were down 26 points at 2,360, a 20.5 point discount to the index.
Brokers said hesitant investors would be keeping an eye on U.S. markets after the U.S. producer price index was released, with Wall Street's reaction likely to set the early local tone next week.
"If the PPI figures are reasonable, U.S. stocks will go up tonight and we will follow suit on Monday," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"But at this stage the market is just very cautious about these figures coming out."
Other market participants agreed. They said the week's local trading was based on second-guessing the Wallis financial system report issued on Wednesday and tonight's U.S. prices report.
"Today has been more of the same. It has been a week of wait and see really," said one broker, hoping for more substantial action next week.
"We may get more of a trend next week."
Features in a day of reluctant trade were hard to find with Victorian-based regional Bank of Melbourne the pick.
The takeover target lost 1.3 percent to A$9.34 as investors fretted over the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's (ACCC) attitude to Westpac Banking Corp's A$9.75 per share bid.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about three to two, while about 33 percent of stockS traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active as players reset positions ahead of U.S. data but options trade was slow.
Total options traded 28,143 (35,730)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 8,370 (6,269)

In other local markets, Australian bonds took the opportunity for a quiet Friday after a week that saw the yield on 10-year bonds move back under 8.00 percent and spreads to U.S. Treasuries come in to two month lows.
By 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.94 percent, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The Australian dollar consolidated its sharp offshore rise, ending the week on a strong note despite a brief consolidative phase during the midsession.
By 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), the local dollar was sitting pretty at US$0.7852/57, having gained an impressive 3/4 of a cent offshore from US$0.7800/05 late here Thursday.
